title: Core: Redesign and refactor Viewports tool
body:
Contributes to https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/33245

## What I did

- Refactored viewports handling into a hook
- Move dimension inputs from toolbar to canvas to reduce clutter
- Updated toolbar Select component to use ActionList components for visual consistency
- Added drag handles to resize the viewport, along with realtime size indicators
- Persist custom size to the URL for sharing

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02ea3391-5b29-48bc-8425-53f1155686d6

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

<!-- Please check (put an "x" inside the "[ ]") the applicable items below to communicate how to test your changes -->

#### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests:

- [x] stories
- [ ] unit tests
- [ ] integration tests
- [ ] end-to-end tests

#### Manual testing

- Use the Viewports tool in the toolbar to switch between viewport presets.
- Try using up/down/enter/esc keys to navigate the menu.
- Try changing the width and height values through the inputs above the iframe.
- Try changing width, height, and both together through the drag handles.
- Try switching orientation through the "swap" button.
- Try resetting the custom size back to the preset through the "undo" button.
- Verify that refreshing the browser will keep the selected viewport.
- Check the other toolbar menus to see if they look okay.

<!-- Please include the steps to test your changes here. For example:

1. Run a sandbox for template, e.g. `yarn task --task sandbox --start-from auto --template react-vite/default-ts`
2. Open Storybook in your browser
3. Access X story

-->

### Documentation

<!-- Please check (put an "x" inside the "[ ]") the applicable items below to indicate which documentation has been updated. -->

- [ ] If you are deprecating/removing a feature, make sure to update
      [MIGRATION.MD](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/next/MIGRATION.md)

## Checklist for Maintainers

- [ ] When this PR is ready for testing, make sure to add `ci:normal`, `ci:merged` or `ci:daily` GH label to it to run a specific set of sandboxes. The particular set of sandboxes can be found in `code/lib/cli-storybook/src/sandbox-templates.ts`
- [ ] Make sure this PR contains **one** of the labels below:
   <details>
     <summary>Available labels</summary>

  - `bug`: Internal changes that fixes incorrect behavior.
  - `maintenance`: User-facing maintenance tasks.
  - `dependencies`: Upgrading (sometimes downgrading) dependencies.
  - `build`: Internal-facing build tooling & test updates. Will not show up in release changelog.
  - `cleanup`: Minor cleanup style change. Will not show up in release changelog.
  - `documentation`: Documentation **only** changes. Will not show up in release changelog.
  - `feature request`: Introducing a new feature.
  - `BREAKING CHANGE`: Changes that break compatibility in some way with current major version.
  - `other`: Changes that don't fit in the above categories.

* **New Features**
  * Right-side "aside" content for select options; new SizeInput control; resizable Viewport with drag-to-resize, numeric inputs, rotate and restore actions; added Viewport stories and watch device icon.

* **Refactor**
  * Viewport tool rebuilt on a centralized hook/state; Select options now render via ActionList; ActionList gains listbox-friendly layouts and two-line title/description items.

* **Style**
  * Improved visuals, focus, hover and active/disabled interaction styling across controls.

**Remove unsafe non-null assertion on `value.type`.**

The `value.type!` assertion is unsafe because the `Viewport` interface defines `type` as optional (`type?: ViewportType`). User-provided viewport configurations can omit this property entirely. Without validation, accessing `iconsMap[undefined]` would fail at runtime. Either validate that type exists before rendering, or provide a default type for viewports missing this property.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In @code/core/src/viewport/components/Tool.tsx at line 30, The code uses an
unsafe non-null assertion on value.type when looking up iconsMap (icon:
iconsMap[value.type!]); update the Tool component to handle a missing type by
either validating value.type before use or falling back to a default
ViewportType (e.g., a DEFAULT_VIEWPORT_TYPE or 'default') and use that for the
iconsMap lookup; ensure references to value.type, iconsMap, and the Tool
rendering logic are updated so no non-null assertion is used and a safe icon is
always selected.
```

</details>

**Fix the viewport dimension parsing to handle non-pixel units.**

The `.replace('px', '')` calls on lines 33 and 35 assume viewport `width` and `height` are always in pixels. However, the `responsiveViewport` (exported from this module) uses `'100%'` for both dimensions, and the viewport system supports custom dimensions with various units (%, em, rem, vw, vh) as documented in the GlobalState type (types.ts line 20).

If the responsive viewport or any custom viewport with non-px units is displayed, these values would render incorrectly (e.g., "100%" instead of a numeric value, or "50em" instead of "50").

Use a more robust unit-stripping approach that handles multiple unit types:

```javascript
const stripUnit = (value: string) => value.replace(/[a-z%]+$/i, '');
// Or conditionally: parseFloat(value).toString()
```

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In @code/core/src/viewport/components/Tool.tsx around lines 31 - 37, The
dimension display in Tool.tsx currently uses value.styles.width.replace('px','')
and value.styles.height.replace('px','') which fails for non-pixel units (e.g.,
'100%', '2em'); update the rendering to strip any trailing CSS unit instead (use
a unit-stripping helper such as a regex that removes trailing letters/percent or
use parseFloat) when rendering inside the Dimensions component so
responsiveViewport and other unit types show the numeric value correctly; update
references to value.styles.width and value.styles.height and add/inline the
stripUnit helper (or use parseFloat) where those spans are produced.
```

</details>

The `muted?: boolean` prop is declared in the type definition but is never used in the component's styling logic. If this prop is intended to control muted text appearance, the styling should conditionally apply based on it. Otherwise, if the `& small` selector is sufficient for muted text styling, consider removing the unused prop to avoid API confusion.



<details>
<summary>🔧 Proposed fix if muted styling is intended</summary>

```diff

+const ActionListText = styled.div<{ muted?: boolean }>(({ theme, muted }) => ({
   display: 'flex',
   flexDirection: 'column',
   justifyContent: 'center',
   flexGrow: 1,
   minWidth: 0,
   padding: '8px 0',
   lineHeight: '16px',
+  color: muted ? 'var(--listbox-item-muted-color)' : 'inherit',
```

Or remove the unused prop:

```diff
+const ActionListText = styled.div(({ theme }) => ({
```

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
If I go to http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/manager-components-preview-viewport--rotated, a bunch of odd things happen:

1. The URL immediately gets `&globals=viewport.isRotated:!undefined` added and stays in the URL
2. The rotate button in the story is not disabled, but does nothing at all
3. The SizeInputs are not disabled, accept input and visually update their value, but do nothing

----
* [x] 1.

This polluted URL bit will stay when you navigate to another page. Compare to http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/addons-docs-blocks-examples-buttonsomeautodocs--forced-bg-light&globals=backgrounds.value:dark.

That forced background story enforces its own value, without resetting the one globally set in the URL. When you navigate to the next story, the globally set dark background is honoured again.

I see the code pattern you used in the story, and I believe it's what's causing the side effect. I'm not sure why you can't set `globals.viewport` on the story like we do elsewhere, but if it's not possible for you, then it won't be possible for our users so we should investigate that.

----

* [x] 2. and 3.

My preference is to behave like the tools in toolbar and disable with a tooltip stating "Viewport set by story, cannot be customized", similarly to how http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/addons-docs-blocks-examples-buttonsomeautodocs--forced-bg-light&globals=backgrounds.value:dark behaves.

If you did want to keep the inputs non-disabled, interacting with them should have an effect on the story rather than do nothing.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: Fixed. There was an issue with `isRotated` getting coerced to `undefined` rather than `false` which is the initial value and therefore will get stripped from the URL as it should be.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: Nice! Does it also fix the issue with `isRotated` persisting to the next story when set on an individual story?

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Reports multiple bugs (polluted URL, disabled button doing nothing, inputs having no effect) and requests specific behavioral fixes including disabling with tooltip.

I think we should address that by creating a "Custom" entry in the select, and making it the selected value whenever users interact with inputs or rotate the viewport. This would shield users from accidental config loss.
